title: Conjugate integral elementary matrices by products of prime dilations
target: gl-n-q-generated-by-gl-n-z-and-prime-dilations

Write `x_ij(r)` (`i != j`, `r in Q`) for the elementary matrix `1 + r E_ij`.

**(2).** `SL_n(Q)` is generated by the `x_ij(r)`, since `Q` is a field. For a
diagonal matrix `t = diag(t_1,...,t_n)` one has
`t x_ij(r) t^-1 = x_ij(t_i t_j^-1 r)`.
- Take `r = a/b` with `a, b in Z`, `b >= 1`, and write `b = ∏ p^(k_p)`.
- For `n >= 3`, put `t = ∏_p d_p^(k_p) = diag(b, b^-1, 1, ..., 1)`. Then
  `t^-1 x_13(1) t = x_13(1/b)`, so `x_13(a/b) = (t^-1 x_13(1) t)^a`.
- For `n = 2`, put `t = diag(b, b^-1)`. Then `t^-1 x_12(1) t = x_12(1/b^2)`,
  so `x_12(a/b) = (t^-1 x_12(1) t)^(ab)`.
- Every other root group is conjugate to `x_13` (or to `x_12` when `n = 2`) by a
  signed permutation matrix in `SL_n(Z)`, which carries `x_13(r)` to some
  `x_ij(±r)`.

So every `x_ij(r)` lies in `<SL_n(Z), d_p : p prime>`.

**(1) and (3).** The map `a -> diag(a,1,...,1)` splits `det: GL_n(Q) -> Q^x`,
so `GL_n(Q) = SL_n(Q) ⋊ D` with `D = {diag(a,1,...,1)}`. By unique
factorization `Q^x = {±1} × ⊕_p p^Z`, so `D = {±1} × E` with `E` free abelian on
the `e_p`, which commute since they are diagonal. `diag(-1,1,...,1)` lies in
`GL_n(Z)`. Finally `d_p = e_p · (w e_p^-1 w^-1)` for the permutation matrix
`w in GL_n(Z)` swapping the first two basis vectors, so
`<GL_n(Z), e_p> ⊇ <SL_n(Z), d_p> = SL_n(Q)`, and together with `D` this gives all
of `GL_n(Q)`. ∎
